slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
Proof of the Pythagorean Theorem by similarity. In right triangle ABC with right angle C, let a = BC, b = AC, c = AB, and let altitude CD split the hypotenuse into AD = x and DB = c − x.

From 9.1: b2 = cx and a2 = c(c − x). Add: a2 + b2 = cx + c2 − cx = c2.

Compare with the area proof in 7.6: that one rearranged pieces; this one uses ratios. Two different chains of reasoning reach the same theorem.

slides.reveal: Triangle ACD and triangle ABC (they share angle A and each has a right angle), so AD/AC = AC/AB.
